extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, program managers, Office of the Chief Communications Officer, Office of Public Engagement, Office of the Chief Information Officer, Congressional appropriations and oversight staff (GAO/OIG)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implementation standards for USPTO operational sub-activities, budget justification, and actions to address GAO/OIG recommendations (particularly for Trademarks, IT security, data, and workforce). Includes milestones, policy changes, and performance target-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Direction, Communication, and Outreach support
rubrics_metrics.description: This funding supports the agency’s leadership, policy development, and public engagement efforts to ensure the USPTO operates effectively and maintains strong relationships with the public and global IP community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds allocated to Office of the Under Secretary and Director, Office of the Chief Communications Officer, and Office of Public Engagement to sustain leadership, policy development, and outreach capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Management Services
rubrics_metrics.description: This funding supports the USPTO’s financial planning, budgeting, accounting, and fee collection operations, which will allow the agency to effectively manage its resources and complies with federal financial standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain compliance with federal financial standards while enabling adequate budgeting, accounting, and fee collection functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resource Management and Administrative Services
rubrics_metrics.description: This funding will enable the USPTO to augment capacity and improve the delivery of the USPTO’s human capital management program, which includes mission-critical positions that must be filled to meet DOC requirements and OPM regulatory changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize filling mission-critical positions and adapting human capital processes to meet Department of Commerce and OPM requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Services support
rubrics_metrics.description: This funding supports the USPTO’s internal legal counsel and regulatory functions, ensuring the agency operates within the bounds of law and sound legal policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain adequate internal legal counsel capacity to support agency regulatory and litigation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase employee engagement and improve CX with streamlined tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernizing and streamlining EBPL’s existing tools and public-facing components will increase employee engagement and customer satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in tool modernization and streamline public-facing components to improve employee experience (EX) and customer experience (CX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect, store, and distribute authoritative data
rubrics_metrics.description: Ingesting, warehousing, and distributing data will lead to greater data maturity and the use of data as an enterprise asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop ingestion, warehousing, and distribution capabilities to raise data maturity and treat data as an enterprise asset; determine standards to ensure integrated, high-quality data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage technology to gain business efficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reducing repetitive manual processes through automation and centralizing tools will save time and costs and increase productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize automation and tool centralization to eliminate repetitive manual work and increase productivity and cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Technology Security objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Security – Protect USPTO systems and data against ever-increasing levels of digital attack, which helps ensure the agency’s continuity of operations and facilitates trust in the integrity of the IP data it’s entrusted with protecting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in security controls and practices that protect systems/data and support continuity of operations and stakeholder trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Technology Resiliency objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Resiliency – Provide continuous operations to customers and to USPTO employees in support of the agency’s mission by maintaining highly available and resilient systems that enable agility and adaptability in delivering business value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain high availability and resiliency of systems to ensure continuous operations and agility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerging Technology objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Emerging Technology – Explore and deliver new capabilities, including cloud, AI, and other solutions to keep pace with customer and USPTO workforce needs, which is paramount in advancing timely decision-making and action to prevent threat actions from negatively impacting the USPTO’s mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and adopt cloud, AI, and other emerging technologies to improve decision-making and operational effectiveness while managing risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Cutting Services/MGE regional office milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening a Southeast Regional Office by December 2025; Establishing the New England Community Outreach Office in Durham, NH; Opening three additional Community Outreach Offices by December 2027, as mandated by UAIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet the stated milestone dates for establishing regional and community outreach offices per statutory mandates (UAIA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and surcharges availability (35 U.S.C. §42(c) and AIA/SUCCESS Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding other provisions, all fees and surcharges assessed and collected by USPTO are available for USPTO only pursuant to section 42(c) of title 35, United States Code, as amended by the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act; AIA and the SUCCESS Act provide fee-setting and surcharge authorities and extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and use fee collections consistent with statutory provisions (AIA, SUCCESS Act, UAIA), including proper handling of excess deposits and spending plans to Committees on Appropriations when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include GAO and OIG unimplemented recommendations in budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The GAO-IG Act requires each agency to include in its annual budget justification a report that identifies each public recommendation issued by GAO and the agency’s OIG that has remained unimplemented for one year or more and provide reconciliation with inspector general SAR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track open recommendations, reconcile with inspector general reports, and include implementation status and action plans in the annual budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document pendency targets and revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop controls to ensure that pendency targets and revisions to the targets are clearly documented and included in any public materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhance documentation of Trademarks budget and reporting policies; OCFO/OPB to outline modifications to pendency targets in budget/performance guidance; adjust public dashboard to display annual pendency targets for prior years as well as current year. Target completion examples: 9/30/25 (doc work), 12/31/24 (dashboard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt long-term trademark pendency goals and communicate them
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a long-term pendency goal that accounts for stakeholder needs to allow for timely business decisions (example: goal of 4.5 months first action and 10 months disposal by FY2027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalize and include long-term application pendency goals in performance and budget documents and communicate to stakeholders (e.g., via TPAC). Target completion: 9/30/25 for some actions; inclusion in FY2025 priorities already begun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set pendency-related KPI targets in strategic and performance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Set targets for the trademark pendency-related KPIs in the 2022–2026 Strategic Plan and include KPIs in the AFR, Annual Performance Plan, Annual Performance Report, and DOC APPR consistent with strategic plan objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per OMB Circular A-11 section 240.1, ensure KPI targets are reflected across required reports. Target completion example: 3/31/26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update trademark production model to include data-driven overtime estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the trademark production model to include supportable, data-driven estimates of overtime usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate empirically supported overtime usage estimates into production modeling. Target example: 6/30/25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalize methodology for estimating and validating efficiency gains
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalize a methodology for estimating and validating efficiency gains before modeling any new efficiency gains in the Trademark production model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not model assumed efficiency gains without a formalized estimation and validation methodology; monitor production and pendency and assess whether efficiency gains should be included. Target example: 9/30/26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and implement a Trademarks workforce action plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a workforce action plan that includes strategies to address challenges in recruitment and retention, milestones, roles of key organization components, measures of success, and a process to continuously assess and revise the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct skills analysis, build on recent recruitment/hiring enhancements, update training initiatives, and implement the plan with milestones. Target examples: analyses and plan milestones with completion dates (6/30/26; 3/31/27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate reporting of IT security incidents (within 1 hour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Align USPTO policy with departmental requirements to have all USPTO employees report all IT security incidents, including PII exposure, immediately (within 1 hour) once an incident is suspected or confirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update Breach Notification Policy to require immediate reporting to SOC; SOC to report to DOC’s Enterprise Operations Center within one hour. Action marked complete with target 5/16/24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish internal controls and training for incident reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an internal control process and provide training to ensure all USPTO employees report IT security incidents immediately (within 1 hour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement two-click reporting from myuspto.gov, update mandatory IT Security Awareness Training with reporting instructions, and update 'Rules of the Road' policy. Target dates provided (various) and actions reported as complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold leadership accountable for incident reporting and risk acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold USPTO leadership accountable for reporting and notification of IT security incidents and to comply with USPTO risk acceptance policies and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide annual small-group briefings to executive leadership by the CISO, implement Incident Reporting Template designating tasks/responsibilities/statuses/outcomes, and update SOC Notification Playbook with defined roles/actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider Privacy Act violations in risk acceptance policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a requirement within USPTO risk acceptance policies and procedures to consider violations of the Privacy Act during IT security incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate Privacy Act considerations into risk acceptance decisions and policies. Action noted complete as of 5/16/24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassess non-mission-critical designation of key systems (e.g., TSDR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reassess the non-mission-critical designation of TSDR and other systems supporting the trademark process and evaluate against DOC HVA checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate evaluations with DOC to determine High Value Assets (HVAs); USPTO reevaluated TSDR and determined it does not meet HVA criteria per OMB M-19-03 (target/completion examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Update log retention policy to federal minimum (2 years, 6 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Update USPTO policy to meet the federal minimum standard of 2 years and 6 months of log retention as established under OMB M-21-31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update Audit, Logging, and Monitoring policy and implement DOC’s minimum event logging requirements. Target examples: policy update completed 5/16/24; full implementation target 9/30/26 for controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fully implement log retention controls per departmental requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect the minimum event logging requirements outlined in OMB M-21-31 and implement log retention controls in USPTO systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement DOC’s 'Incident Response Management Standard v1.1' conditions and comply with log collection, retention, and monitoring standards. Action status: In-Progress with target 9/30/26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and align public commitments and masking policy for trademark data
rubrics_metrics.description: Update System of Records Notice, the Trademark Manual of Examining Procedure (TMEP), and public commitments so that they are all consistent regarding what data will not be publicly viewable; interim clarification that certain fields are masked as a courtesy and not private.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue Federal Register Notice to change masking policy, unmask owner email and attorney bar information fields, and amend TMEP to delete masking references; actions staged with target dates (some complete, others in-progress).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and conduct regular fraud risk assessments of the trademark register
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and conduct regular fraud risk assessments to determine a fraud risk profile that aligns with leading practices in the Fraud Risk Framework, including identifying inherent fraud risks, assessing likelihood and impact, determining fraud risk tolerance, examining existing fraud controls, and documenting the fraud risk profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update Trademarks fraud risk framework and conduct annual assessments; incorporate analytics and controls to mitigate suspicious activities. Target example: update completed by 9/30/24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve data systems and analytics for stronger fraud risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and implement improvements to current data systems to strengthen trademark data analytics for stronger fraud risk management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhance analytics platform, ingest and catalog transactional data, determine data standards, curate transactional data for predictive modeling and consistent analysis, and leverage analytics in the Register Protection Office. Target examples: various completion/in-progress dates through 12/31/26 and 9/30/26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure budgeting/transparency for reprogrammed and excess fee funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If amounts received in excess of the appropriated sum are deposited in the Patent and Trademark Fee Reserve Fund, those amounts remain available until expended, but the Director must submit a spending plan to the Committees on Appropriations which shall be treated as a reprogramming under section 504.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reprogramming requires compliance with section 504 procedures; reprogrammed amounts must be transferred to 'Salaries and Expenses' and reflected in the President’s budget for subsequent fiscal year if expected increases result from fee changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track implementation status and target completion dates for GAO/OIG recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: For each GAO/OIG recommendation, present Action(s) Planned, Action Status (Planned/In-Progress/Complete), Target Completion Date, and Recommendation Status in the budget justification Exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Exhibit reporting format to show per-recommendation actions, status, and target dates (examples throughout Exhibit 41).
